title: Chiller-1 Chilled Water Supply Sensor Slowly Drifting High
description: Chiller-1 is running normally and proven, but its CHWS Temp sensor begins drifting upward over several minutes -- a classic slow-onset sensor calibration failure rather than a sudden fault, meant to be caught by trending rather than an alarm.

events.description: CHWS Temp begins drifting upward at 0.02 F/s (~1.2 F/min) after the chiller has had time to prove and settle near setpoint

expected_results: Chiller-1 CHWS Temp reads normally (near 44F) for the first two minutes
CHWS Temp then climbs gradually and continuously rather than jumping or oscillating
Chiller Status remains proven/OK throughout -- this is a sensor problem, not an equipment failure
Downstream cooling performance should appear to degrade slowly, mimicking a real fouled/miscalibrated sensor
completion_criteria: Student notices the drift via a trend rather than a single reading
Student differentiates this from a real loss-of-cooling-capacity fault (chiller status, flow, and enable/command points remain normal)
instructor_notes: Good scenario for teaching trend usage specifically -- a single point-in-time reading a few minutes in doesn't look obviously wrong.
student_objectives: Use trend data, not just a single point read, to catch a slow-onset sensor fault
Correctly rule out equipment failure when only a sensor is at fault
